questions.text: Which of the following, a non-flammable noble gas named for the Greek sun god, is the second-lightest element on the periodic table?
An isotope is an atom that has a different number of neutrons—and thus a different mass number—than another atom of the same element. Which choice below names an isotope of carbon?
Which pair of values below shows the boiling point of water in both Celsius and Fahrenheit temperature scales?
Match each substance to its approximate pH value.

The diagram at right shows the stopping distances of two identical cars on two different surface conditions. If their initial velocities were the same, what force caused the second car's distance to be much greater than the first car's?
When a projectile is fired into the air, it follows a predictable arc. What is the name for the shape of that arc?
When an object that produces sound is moving towards you, the sound waves are compressed, making the pitch higher than normal. What is this phenomenon called, as illustrated in the diagram?

When a simple machine is used to reduce the amount of work to move an object, the efficiency ratio is called the mechanical advantage. If an included plane (ramp) is 8 feet long and 2 feet high, what is the mechanical advantage when using the ramp to lift the object?

Visible light has a wavelength ranging from about 400 to 700 nanometers. Which of the following is about the same size as the wavelength of visible light? the height of this capital T, water molecules, the width of a soccer field, small bacteria
There are three methods of heat transfer. Match each type of heat transfer to its description.
Which of the following is an example of an ecosystem's biotic factor? precipitation, temperature, soil chemistry, decomposer
Below are four astronomers. Which one revolutionized the field by proposing the heliocentric model of the solar system? Galileo Galilei, Nicolaus Copernicus, Tycho Brahe, Johannes Kepler
On the Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram, it encompasses about 90% of the universe's stars. Which of the following categories currently includes our sun?

NASA conducted the Mariner flybys, set Viking into orbit, and sent rovers called "Pathfinder," "Spirit," "Opportunity," and "Curiosity" to study it. What planet is home to Olympus Mons, and is orbited by Phobos and Deimos?
After discovering it, Edwin Hubble used its existence as proof that the universe is expanding. What names the electromagnetic phenomenon that occurs when an object moves farther away from earth?
This behaviorist experimented in the realm of classical conditioning. He was able to trigger a conditioned reflex in dogs. Who is this physiologist?

The fight-or-flight response in organisms causes a surge of this hormone to enter the bloodstream, helping to adjust to sudden stress. It was isolated by John Abel in 1897, and is also known as epinephrine. What is the hormone that causes rapid heart rate and an increase in energy?

In a mammalian womb, a baby receives nourishment from this organ that is attached to the uterine wall. It is expelled from the uterus once the baby is born. What is the name of the organ that is connected to the embryo via the umbilical cord?
In the genotype of an organism, a gene can be referred to as heterozygous. Which of the following genotypes refers to a heterozygous condition for a gene? P, PP, pp, Pp
The four nucleotide bases of DNA pair up in specific ways. The base pairs of RNA behave in a similar way. Match the nucleotide on the left with the base it pairs with in DNA or RNA.
In November 2022, the UN marked what milestone in the Earth’s population?
Aves is a class of organisms that are warm-blooded, egg-laying vertebrates. Which of these animals belongs to the aves class? chameleon, sparrow, frog, platypus

In the natural world, availability of water, food, shelter and space are all conditions that affect populations. Additionally, human development and over-hunting can skew the predator-prey balance. What is the collective term for these conditions which keep animal populations under control?

Symbiotic relationships are interactions between two different animal species. An example of this is a remora riding attached to a shark, feeding on the sharks’ leftovers. What specific type of symbiosis is this?

In Alaska, tours are often given around glaciers, with guests hoping to see a piece of a glacier break off into the water. Marked by a distinctive cracking sound, what is the process of a glacier separating called?

This natural phenomenon exists due to movement of molecules from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure. What is this phenomenon that can be measured by an anemometer, and be given a value on the Beaufort scale?

This biome is also known as the boreal forest. Trees in this region are generally coniferous. What is the biome that spans Russia and Canada, and is found just south of the tundra region in the northern hemisphere?

A national park in Montana is named for these formations. One of these is part of the source of the Yangtze River in China. Which geological features below cover a little over 10% of the Earth’s surface?
Convergent, divergent, and transform are three types of movement of tectonic plates. With what natural phenomenon are these plate boundaries most associated?
Match each star’s name to its description.
The Big Dipper is an asterism, or a pattern of stars, which is found inside of a larger constellation. What is this constellation, whose name means “Larger Bear” in Latin?

Perseid, Leonid, and Geminid are the names of these types of celestial events that have annual “peak” times. They are often caused by the dust released from comets. What cosmic events are being described?

Some botanists equate this plant process to sweating in humans. It is the process by which plants lose water vapor through stomata in their leaves. What is this process, from the Latin for “breathe across”?

This drupe was named by Spanish explorers because it resembles a monkey face. It provides a nutritious source of meat, juice, milk and oil that has fed and nourished populations worldwide for generations. What is this edible plant product?

Chicle is a substance that is used in the food service industry, though originally it was used in an attempt to make synthetic rubber. What product is created with chicle, which is extracted from the sapodilla tree?
When buried plant material is exposed to groundwater rich in dissolved solids over a period of millions of years, this is formed. What is this type of fossilized remains?

Common in warm, tropical areas, these parasites usually live in the intestines. Some of the infections caused by these parasites are ascariasis, river blindness, and trichinosis. What are these parasites (also called nematodes) often caused by poor sanitation and hygiene?
Which of the following is the correct order for taxonomic rankings, following Domain and Kingdom?

cards.answer: Phylum Class Order Family Genus Species

questions.text: Mammals and birds have two ventricles in their heart. These are the lower sections of the heart that receive blood from the atria. How many ventricles do amphibians and fish generally have?
Specialized features of animals can be comprised of unique material. Match each animal’s feature to what it is made of.
A virus’s genetic material is protected by this protein shell. It also detects cells suitable for infection, and opens target cells to initiate infection. What is this shell known as?
This process can be completed by either the lytic cycle or the lysogenic cycle. What is the process by which DNA is transferred, by a virus, from one bacterium to another?

An operating system is software that allows a computer, tablet, or other device to become usable, and run other software. Which of these is an example of an operating system? Windows 10, Google, iPhone X, TikTok

The HMS Beagle gained notoriety in its second voyage, when this naturalist joined the expedition. The mission had multiple objectives, including surveying and charting coastlines, and studying geology and zoology of lands visited. Who was the famous naturalist, and author of “The Origin of Species”?
An ichthyologist is a scientist that studies a specific group. Which of these would be of interest to an ichthyologist? a trout, a tarantula, a volcano, a vulture
SpaceX, Tesla, Neuralink, PayPal, and OpenAI were all founded or co-founded by the same person. Who is this billionaire that has his sights set on visiting Mars?

In the human body, you’ll find these tubes, some of which are named femoral, subclavian, and carotid. What are the blood vessels that carry oxygenated blood away from the heart, to the cells and organs of the body?
Aside from quinine, this is the only drug that is either naturally present in, or added to, widely consumed foods. What is the mildly addictive drug that can be found in chocolate, sodas, and tea?

BMI stands for Body Mass Index. It is calculated by taking a person’s weight in kilograms, and divide by the square of their height in meters. If a BMI value is over 30, what does this indicate about a person?
Different vitamins can benefit the human body, and prevent ailments. Match each vitamin to its preventative measure.
